solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Blow, with socialists imposing sanction on House

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the approval word follows the house abbreviation

parts.note: the political left is the socialist wing
to OK something is to sanction or approve it

explanation.surface: A political attack: socialists forcing a penalty on the House of Commons is quite a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing punch thrown with the leading arm in a curving swing is this kind of blow.

clue.text: Politician's mounting anger over African extremists from Monrovia?

parts.note: a Lib is a Liberal politician

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means rising, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: extremists are the end letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A politician growing angry about African radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns IRE into ERI; 'extremists' takes AN from African.
explanation.definitionFit: Monrovia is the capital of Liberia, so a native of it belongs to that West African nation.

clue.text: Chef is doubly inept, holding large kitchen utensil

indicators.note: holding means one piece clasps another inside it
inept means clumsy or badly done, so these letters are jumbled
doubly means the word is used twice over

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: A clumsy chef dropping a big kitchen utensil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' means 'is' is used twice in the anagram pool; 'holding' then wraps the result around the large sign.
explanation.definitionFit: This broad slotted spatula is a cooking implement for turning and lifting fish.

clue.text: Introductions from Horatio Lord Nelson?

parts.note: the opening letters of the name Horatio

explanation.surface: Asking for introductions from the admiral Horatio, Lord Nelson.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson here is not the admiral but a wrestling move, as in full nelson.
explanation.definitionFit: A nelson is a wrestling grip applied under the arms and behind the neck, an example of such a grip.

clue.text: When can I lie about with nothing on top? Not very often

indicators.note: on top means placed first in a down entry

parts.note: O is the zero digit, nothing

indicators.note: about signals the words are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Wondering when one can lie around naked, which is rarely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing on top' suggests nudity, but places the zero at the head of the anagram signalled by 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means occasionally, at long intervals, so rarely.

clue.text: Investigated mood of tired person?

definitions.meaning: looked into closely, as a detective does
a weary person is in favour of (pro) going to bed

explanation.surface: Asking what a tired person's mood is, as if it were a matter for inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word as PRO-BED: someone tired is all for bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe a matter is to examine it searchingly, so the past tense matches investigated.

clue.text: Changes in Soviet behaviour

parts.note: red is the colour associated with Soviet communism
one's actions are one's behaviour

explanation.surface: Shifts in how the Soviet Union behaved.
explanation.definitionFit: Editorial revisions, especially cuts of sensitive material from documents, are alterations made to a text.

clue.text: Magnate put up in a manor abroad

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means raised, so the letters read upwards
in means the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: A tycoon staying in a manor house overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds NORAB in 'manor abroad'; 'put up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a powerful businessman, as in a press or oil tycoon.

clue.text: Bold group of American lawyers

parts.note: a DA is an American district attorney
a ring is a group or gang

explanation.surface: A daring band of US attorneys.
explanation.definitionFit: Courageous and willing to take risks, as a bold adventurer is.

clue.text: Bishop, one in Calais reformed church

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: reformed signals the letters are shaped into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A bishop in Calais presiding over a church that has been reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' sounds ecclesiastical in the surface, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, especially one given special status by the Pope.

clue.text: I love seeing king and queen at a special event

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
R stands for rex, Latin for king
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to see the royal couple turn up at a gala.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is what such a person might say of themselves: an adorer is one who declares 'I love'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adorer is a devoted admirer, someone whose stance is summed up by saying they love.

clue.text: Animal, very fast, first of all caught bird

parts.note: to collar a suspect is to catch them; first of all puts this piece at the start

indicators.note: fast means fixed firmly, so one piece is held tight inside another

parts.note: a doe is a female deer

explanation.surface: An animal running very fast catches a bird first of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but means held fast: V is secured inside DOE.
explanation.definitionFit: This pale grey dove with a black neck band is a common garden bird in Europe.

clue.text: Growth of cereal under discussion

indicators.note: being discussed means being spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: rye is a cereal grain; ryes, or rye's, is said like the answer

explanation.surface: Talking about how much a cereal crop has grown.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase in size or amount, such as a pay increase, is a growth in it.

clue.text: Clergyman from Spanish island? No, French

parts.note: Minorca is one of the Balearic Islands
non is French for no

explanation.surface: Asking whether a clergyman comes from a Spanish island, and being told no, he is French.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor canon is a cathedral clergyman who assists in services but is not a member of the chapter.

clue.text: Indicating cement work on walls of apartment

parts.note: pointing is filling brick joints with mortar

indicators.note: walls of means the outside letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Signs of mortar repairs on the outer walls of a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Directing a finger towards something is a way of showing it.

clue.text: Sort of fab girl that I love? Not half

definitions.text: Sort of fab girl that I love? Not half

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to arrange, so the following letters are put in order anew
only half of the word love is kept, its first two letters

explanation.surface: An admirer describing the kind of fab girl they love, adding the British 'not half!' meaning 'absolutely'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' anagrams FAB GIRL THAT I plus LO, the first half of LOVE ('Not half').
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an attractive person, the very sort of fabulous girl someone could fall for.

clue.text: Top fixer sorted out Irish deal

indicators.note: sorted out means rearranged, so these letters are put in new order

explanation.surface: A senior fixer settling an Irish business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip that holds hair in place on the head is a fixer for the top.

clue.text: Worried a soldier's declared missing at the outset

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: the first letter is missing from the word

parts.note: stated means declared

explanation.surface: Anxiety after a soldier was announced missing at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agitated is being anxious and disturbed, the state of the worried.

clue.text: Stand good chance of being chosen to participate in race?

definitions.text: Stand good chance of being chosen
definitions.meaning: to be a serious contender for a job or prize
literally to be among the runners in a race

explanation.definitionFit: Being a live contender for selection, or literally being one of the runners in a contest.

clue.text: Threaten mischief maker with death!

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
one's end is one's death

explanation.surface: A melodramatic warning to a troublemaker that death awaits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that impends looms or hangs over, menacing as a coming danger does.

clue.text: Gosh! Quite a bit of publicity for plugging musical

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise like gosh

indicators.note: plugging means filling a hole, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: fairly means quite, to a moderate degree
an advertisement, or ad, is a bit of publicity

explanation.surface: Surprise at how much publicity is being used to plug a musical show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugging' suggests promoting the show, but signals insertion into the word for quite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lerner and Loewe stage show based on Shaw's Pygmalion is a famous musical.

clue.text: Regularly showing flair, one's picked up a foreign language

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken
picked up in a down clue means lifted, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: one is I, and 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone with a flair for languages picking one up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' gives I + S (one is); 'picked up' reverses it to SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Farsi is the Persian language spoken in Iran, foreign to English speakers.

clue.text: Listen to me removing articles from Volkswagen

indicators.note: removing says letters are taken out of the car's name

parts.note: the Passat is a Volkswagen car model
a and a are two indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Someone demanding attention while stripping parts out of a Volkswagen.
explanation.definitionFit: This hissed sound is used to attract attention quietly, as if saying come and hear this.

clue.text: Maybe saw plunder being lifted

indicators.note: being lifted in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: loot is plunder

explanation.surface: Perhaps stolen goods were seen being carried off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the past of see; it is the cutting implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is one example of a hand implement used for work.

clue.text: Anger as English harvest suffers setback, ultimately failing

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the letters are read right to left
the last letter of the harvest word fails, so it is dropped

parts.note: to garner is to gather in, as a harvest

explanation.surface: Farmers furious that the English harvest has failed in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately failing' cuts GARNER to GARNE; 'suffers setback' turns EGARNE round.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage someone is to make them furious, so it means the verb anger.

clue.text: One drives over hill covered in fog

indicators.note: covered in means one piece sits inside the other, wrapped around

parts.note: mist is a thin fog
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone driving over a hilltop blanketed in fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who drives a car is a car driver, the one who drives in the definition.

clue.text: After start of December, first terrible problems with snow

indicators.note: start of points to the opening letter of the next word
terrible here means badly mangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Since early December there have been awful snow problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' reads as an ordinary adverb but is the fodder that 'terrible' shuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaps of snow piled up by wind block roads and cause winter trouble.

clue.text: Literate learners were about to get a mediocre grade

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plates on cars; two learners give LL
a D is a poor school or exam grade

explanation.surface: Students who were about to receive a poor mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone widely educated through books is literate in the fullest sense.
